newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany wants extradition of Northern Irish suspect.
newsitem.headline: Germany wants extradition of Northern Irish suspect.

text.p: Germany said on Monday it had asked Northern Ireland to extradite the daughter of former Irish nationalist member of the British parliament Bernadette McAliskey on suspicion of involvement in a mortar attack on a British army base.
A spokesman for the federal prosecutor's office in Karlsruhe said the extradition request for Roisin McAliskey had been issued by Germany's federal court.
"I can confirm that an arrest warrant has been issued," the spokesman said. "She is a strong suspect."
Police want to question McAliskey about an Irish Republican Army (IRA) attack near the northwestern town of Osnabrueck in June.
The blast from the attack caused no injuries but blew out the windows of cars and nearby buildings, including a Catholic chapel.
Northern Irish police confirmed they had received an extradition request from Germany but declined to name the person involved.
"The German authorities are in touch with us regarding their inquiries into serious terrorist crime in their jurisdiction," said a spokeswoman for the Royal Ulster Constabulary.
"A woman is currently in custody in Northern Ireland and an extradition warrant has been sworn by the German authorities in London this morning," the police spokeswoman said.
McAliskey's mother, better known as Bernadette Devlin, a leading figure in Northern Irish civil rights marches during the 1960s.
She became the youngest woman to be elected -- as an independent -- to the British parliament when she took her seat on her 22nd birthday in 1969. She held it until 1974
The BBC said her daughter had been in police custody for six days.
